note: Read 2026-10-30: the Road Traffic Act, Cap. 7.06, revised edition showing the law at 1 January 2025 (the Government of Montserrat's PDF of February 2026). Section 35(b): a private driver's licence lets its holder drive, not for reward, the vehicles the driving test proves them competent to drive. Section 39(1)(c): a person is disqualified for holding or obtaining a driver's licence for a private motor car under 17; the learner's permit (section 34(3), a separate permission, also from 17 for a motor vehicle) isn't a driver's licence, so 17 is the licence's own age by the Act. Section 41: a driver's licence is valid three years from the holder's birthday in the year of issue (held as 3 years; the birthday alignment the form doesn't hold). Schedule 1, Part C: a private driver's licence costs EC$150 (held), with a driver's licence processing fee of EC$100 and the written (EC$30) and road (EC$50) tests on top (not held: the form holds the licence's own fee); a holder of a valid foreign licence (other than an OECS one) may apply without a test for EC$650 (section 38(3)(b); from any country, so not held as an exchange list). The Licensing Officer is the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry responsible for public works (section 2, inserted by Act 12 of 2021); the Division is named in the Government's notice of 8 March 2023 launching its online licence system. No identity card is issued under the Act.
